To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weathering of granitic rocks in Cameroon is characterized by the formation of kaolinite, illite, gibbsite, goethtie and maghemite; quartz and K-felderpar are etched by chemical action; etched pit densities on residual quartz surfaces increase with increasing weathering.
the chemical weathering of granitic rocks in Cameroon has led to the formation of kaolinite and illitic minerals.

the etched pits recorded on residual quartz grains from kaolinized granite rocks are the result of the combined effects of the chemical dissolution of quartz and the subsequent removal of the etched material from the quartz surface by chemical and mechanical processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the weathering processes and the origin of etch pits recorded on residual grain surfaces in granitic rocks.
the weathering processes of granitic rocks in West region of Cameroon.
the weathering of granite rocks in the West region of Cameroon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
etching is a result of chemical action of the pore fluids on the residual quartz and K-felspar grains, and the etch pit densities on quartz grains reflect weathering intensity.
etching of quartz surfaces is due to chemical weathering.
the origin of the etch pits on the residual quartz and K-felspar grains is mainly due to the dissolution and precipitation of quartz and kaolinite in the pore fluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical weathering of the granitic rocks in West Cameroon was characterized by the dissolution of quartz and feldspar, with the formation of kaolinite and illites as the main products.

the weathering processes of the studied granitic rocks in West Cameroon have resulted in the formation of kaolinite and illites as the most abundant weathering products, and the formation of etch pits on the residual quartz and feldspar surfaces.
kaolinite and illites are the most important products of weathering of granitic rocks in West Region Cameroon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the etched pit densities on the surfaces of quartz and K-fledspar grains can be used as a proxy to estimate the degree of chemical weathering of granitic rocks.
the etching of quartz grains in kaolinized rocks can be attributed to the chemical action of pore fluids.
etching of quartz surfaces can be used to estimate weathering rates of granitic rocks in tropical regions.
